scope: M7-M9 native ownership, benchmark phase boundaries, clean build/runtime procedure

findings.finding: Prepared resident_ns originally included a clock gap excluded from planning_ns=0 and execution_ns.
findings.fix: Prepared ready is start, so resident_ns equals execution_ns; resident planning plus execution sums exactly.

findings.finding: Resident validation used Engine::query while timing used fresh Engine::prepare plus execute.
findings.fix: Both validation and measurement now use fresh prepare plus execute with the same owning sink.

ownership_review: Prepared AST destroyed before its retained Memory owner; weak catalog identity prevents stale catalog execution.
All bound descriptor/read state reset at execution start; Result and fresh operators independent across trials.
Failed load preserves catalog token and previous prepared plan; successful load invalidates old plan.
Engine is single-threaded; prepared plan execution does not promise concurrent safety.
fairness_review: Same column storage, physical right hash join, owning result sink and baseline counters; optional profiling disabled.
Full validation results precede timings; no digest-only correctness.
Result and temporary resident-plan destruction occur outside stated timing; this is disclosed.
Warmup and recorded trials interleave via saved seeded Fisher-Yates schedule; all repeats retained.
Engine-lifetime accounted peaks include prior trials and retained prepared plans, not isolated per-query memory/RSS.
limitations: Bounded deterministic mutation fuzzing is not coverage-guided fuzzing.
Injected allocation failures cover PMR accounted allocations, not all process allocations.
Linux and hosted macOS CI jobs are configured but have not run.
macOS LeakSanitizer unsupported; ASan/UBSan final gates remain required.
final_findings_validation: Both native timing findings passed protocol regressions under Debug/Release/ASan+UBSan and both complete final profiles
